title: Kenyan Grilled Goat Skewers
community: Popular across Kenya — with Swahili roots
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Mishkaki ya Mbuzi — Kenyan Grilled Goat Skewers — tender cubes of goat marinated in garlic, ginger, lemon, and spices then charcoal-grilled until smoky and juicy. Many consider goat mishkaki the superior version — richer and more flavourful than beef.
longDesc: Goat mishkaki is often considered the traditional version of this classic Swahili street food — goat has been herded along the East African coast for centuries, long before beef became widely accessible. The richer flavour and slightly firmer texture of goat hold up beautifully to the charcoal and the spiced marinade.
ingredients: 700g boneless goat — leg or shoulder, cut into 2—3 cm cubes
steps: Combine all marinade ingredients. Add the goat cubes and mix well.
Marinate for at least 2 hours — overnight is best.
Thread goat cubes onto skewers with small gaps.
Grill over glowing charcoal for 12—18 minutes, turning every 4 minutes.
Goat takes slightly longer than beef — check one piece by cutting open. The inside should be just cooked through with no pink.
chefTips: Goat takes slightly longer than beef to cook through on skewers — allow an extra 3—5 minutes.
Leg meat is ideal — more flavourful and holds its shape on the skewer.
The longer the marinade, the better the result with goat.
commonMistakes: Undercooking — goat must be cooked through, not served pink like beef.
Cutting pieces too large — they take too long to cook evenly.

faqs.q: Should goat be fully cooked through?
faqs.a: Yes — unlike beef, goat is best fully cooked rather than served pink. Well-cooked goat is still juicy and tender, especially from the leg or shoulder.

cookingScience: Goat has less intramuscular fat than beef, which means it dries out more quickly if overcooked. The marinade — particularly the oil and acid from lemon juice — helps retain moisture during grilling by coating the surface and slightly denaturing the outer proteins.
sustainabilityTips: Goat is one of the most sustainable red meat choices.
reheating: Reheat in oven at 180°C for 5—7 minutes.
healthBenefits: Lean protein — goat has less fat than beef or lamb.
culturalNote: Goat mishkaki is the traditional version of this iconic Swahili street food, with roots going back centuries to the coastal trade routes that brought marinated skewered meat to East Africa.
